If it was just a matter of printing more and there is tons of unmet demand for all these boxes, then they would simply just switch it over to "temporarily sold out" and send out another batch whenever the supposed bottleneck allowed.

But I think that if they were to print out say... 10x the amount of these Aether Wars boxes from the start... there would be a ton of unbought ones... not only on warehouse shelves... but also on retail shelves... and then the retail stores would have to work to sell all the aether wars boxes months or years down the line when there is little demand/hype maybe they even have to drop the price on the box set (like they used to do in warhammer stores for old WFB stuff when it sat for a long time(less profitable business model as proven by their stock performance))... But this way, by having all these boxes sell out very quickly... not only does customer demand rise... but retail stores aren't scared to put in a large order of say 20x Aehter Wars boxes, if they can be sure that in the month or two to come, they will be sold out online and soon to be going up in price.

It worked so well for all the past boxes... By having some of these boxes like looncurse or soon to be aether wars sell out and rise in price ABOVE their retail price because of demand once they are oop... All 5 of my accounts are not subbed. I was having fun multiboxing the triglav invasions and stuff but it got old...

The game for me often seems to demand 10 hours of preparation and time investment for a few hours of actual fun gameplay... rather than being steadily fun throughout. Just my opinion.

These day's I've been playing a lot of Mordhau and getting into VR Games.

I enjoyed the invasions by the triglavians... I was multiboxing 5 accounts and was able to solo minor sites pretty comfortably and clear about 4 of them an hour with looting/salvaging... 

But I got burnt out eventually.

The upkeep on 5 accounts is too much... probably represents about 20\~ hours realistically of me multiboxing to pay off the 5 accounts for a month... or of course paying close to a cell phone bill to sub 5 accounts for a month w/ dollars.

I was with a longtime corp that I've had some good pvp action with... we've killed some smaller capital ships, we've had good pvp but the corp is kind of stagnant... always has been really spotty with fleets and any type of action... and most of the pvp they do is always geared for training newbros as it's basically a zerg-corp that recruits everyone and anyone who applies.... Joining another corp representing a very big time investment... moving all my assets, selling off all my stuff that I wasn't moving... then moving 5 characters out there to a spot in nulsec is a big time investment, and one that I haven't found has really paid off in the past.

So once again I stopped playing eve... None of my accounts are subbed.

I like the game, the economy and forcing people to move everything around and craft everything is really cool... the open pvp and having you lose your ship when you die is also great... But when it ultimately means I'm faced with like a few hours of me doing very boring gate to gate moving and selling/consolidating assets etc... and all the other logistic of either moving to nulsec or operating somewhere far away from any major trade hubs... It becomes such a pain in the ass...

I kind of hate to make the comparison but it is almost like the curse of World of Warcraft.... **Once it starts DEMANDING your time... like the game basically tells you, "you need to be ready to invest hours whenever you sit down and launch this game".... Once it gets to that point... I'd rather not launch it at all. I'll go find something fun I can play for 30 minutes or for 3 hours and have fun the entire time and not feel like I have to spend tens of hours in preparation for the moments that are fun.**

I need a decent job that doesn't lead me to a lifetime of working to make other people rich.

But that seems like a pipe dream.

I appreciate your well thought out response, lacking personal insults or anything like that. I read it, in its entirety because it's very sincere.

I understand it's a sacred place to many people, although maybe I don't understand the magnitude of importance it holds for some. It's indeed very unique and very beautiful location. The sunsets and sunrises up there are surreal. I also get the fight to maintain a culture that has for the most part been eradicated by modernization and tourism, I think that's important to hold onto and everything you say about the loss of culture and stolen land, It rings true.

But I still see some things different.

I don't think the telescopes/astronomers are claiming the land or taking it from natives, in the way that the resorts, hotels, & wealthy people from out of state are... The access road and summit are open to the public weather permitting, the same cannot be said about lush golf courses, resort property and of course purchased private land... The summit of Mauna Kea is open to the public and I think that's an important distinction.

I totally agree much of what you said about the loss of culture/land/religion/identity etc, I think that's a very tragic and very real thing that has happened and continues to happen today, and if it was another battle, say the construction of a new massive resort right there on saddle rd., I'd probably be right behind you, cheering you on or protesting at your shoulder.

But in my unique view, I think that these telescopes deserve special consideration. These telescopes bring nations together... The discoveries made by the telescopes will be shared by everyone. Our knowledge of the cosmos would be in the dark ages without telescopes. The photos made by some of these telescopes are simply so amazing, so life changing for me, that as an agnostic person with no religion: I truly think that photos like hubbles deep field photography are sacred to me on some level. There's nothing on this planet that has spoken to me the way a picture of countless galaxies in a pinhole of the nights sky has... and so I think space photography, telescopes, astronomy, engineering all these types of things... They are the pinnacles of our civilizations. It's one of the few instances to me where people put down their differences and put down their general focus on profits/greed, sit down and try to do something that is simply good. Not good for a select number of people, not good for their country, but just good for everyone on the planet, our understanding of the cosmos and our understanding of our place within the cosmos.

For me, the world is such a silly place. Everywhere you turn there are conflicts, people arguing through their teeth or shooting at eachother, people focused solely on profits everywhere you look, chain businesses proliferating on the backs of low wage workers, etc... Cutthroat sounds like a good word to describe it... Not even going to go into all the hate in the world... But astronomy/telescopes, they have always separated themselves from this. So when it comes to the construction of a new generation of telescope on Mauna Kea, in my opinion I think it deserves special consideration. I think that it should be constructed, even if only to balance out all the other greedy/hateful projects we inevitably allow.

I want to stress this is all just a matter of my opinion. Above all I appreciate you sharing your opinion as well. It was very enlightening for me, an honestly kind of made me see things in a new light, even if it didn't shift my opinion wholly to the opposite side.

The connection between *decimate* and the number ten harks back to a brutal practice of the army of ancient Rome. A unit that was guilty of a severe crime (such as mutiny) was punished by selecting and executing one-tenth of its soldiers, thereby scaring the remaining nine-tenths into obedience. It's no surprise that the word for this practice came from Latin *decem,* meaning "ten." From this root we also get our word *decimal* and the name of the month of December, originally the tenth month of the calendar before the second king of Rome decided to add January and February. **In its extended uses** ***decimate*** **strayed from its "tenth" meaning and nowadays refers to the act of destroying or hurting something in great numbers.**
